inline_comments.comment: Both `getComponentCandidates` and `runGhostStories` are now exported from `storybook/internal/core-server` (added in `code/core/src/core-server/index.ts` in this very PR). Importing them via deep relative paths across package boundaries (`../../../code/core/src/...`) is fragile and bypasses the public API surface. Use `import { getComponentCandidates, runGhostStories } from 'storybook/internal/core-server'` instead, which is the pattern used in `scripts/eval/lib/grading-helpers.test.ts`.

`parseGitDiffStatus` silently returns `'M'` for any status code it doesn't recognize. Git has additional status codes that a renamed/modified project could produce: `'C'` (copied), `'T'` (type change), `'U'` (unmerged), and `'X'` (unknown). Classifying these as 'M' (modified) distorts the `fileChanges` report. Either extend the allowlist or fall back to a sentinel like `'M'` with an inline comment acknowledging the known gap.

`'summary' in result` is an unnecessary duck-type check. `TestRunSummary.summary` is already typed as optional (`summary?: { total: number; ... }`), so TypeScript narrows it correctly with a plain `result.summary` access. Replace `const summary = 'summary' in result ? result.summary : undefined;` with `const summary = result.summary;` — this is clearer and avoids the misleading implication that the property might not exist on the type at all.

The `catch` block in `readCacheInfo` silently swallows all errors and returns `undefined`. Per project rules, catch blocks must not be empty — they must log at minimum at debug level. A JSON parse failure (e.g., corrupted cache file) or an unexpected `readFile` error (EACCES, EISDIR) is indistinguishable from a legitimately missing file. At a minimum: `catch (e) { logger.debug(`Cache info read failed: ${e}`); return undefined; }`. Note that `logger` would need to be threaded in.

The `catch` block in `captureEnvironment` suppresses all errors with only a comment. This hides real problems: if `git` is not on `PATH`, or the harness is run from a directory with unexpected permissions, the error is silently dropped and `evalBranch`/`evalCommit` are recorded as `'unknown'` with no diagnostic. Log the error at debug level so failures surface during troubleshooting.

`const effort = variant.effort as 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'max'` is a redundant cast. After the `if (variant.agent !== 'claude') throw` guard on line 12, TypeScript narrows `variant` to the `{ agent: 'claude'; effort: ClaudeEffort }` branch, and `ClaudeEffort` is already defined as `'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'max'`. Remove the `as` cast.

`debug: true` is hardcoded in the shared AGENTS config with no way to toggle it per-run. The Claude Agent SDK's debug mode produces verbose low-level output that will appear in every eval run's logs regardless of the `--verbose` flag. Consider deriving this from the `verbose` option passed to the trial, or at least document why always-on debug mode is intentional for the eval harness.

`citty` is added as a dependency but is not imported or used anywhere in this PR. `eval.ts` uses `parseArgs` from `node:util` for CLI argument parsing, and no other new file imports `citty`. This is a dead dependency — remove it.

The `generate-and-run-config` job is upgraded from `small` to `large` resource class with no comment or PR description entry explaining why. `large` costs roughly 4× more credits than `small`. If this change is required (e.g., OOM errors or excessive duration), add an inline comment documenting the reason so future maintainers don't inadvertently revert it or keep it unnecessarily.

There is no overall timeout on `driver.execute(...)`. An unresponsive agent (network stall, infinite tool-call loop) will block the trial indefinitely. Consider wrapping the call with `Promise.race([driver.execute(...), timeout(MAX_TRIAL_MS)])` or propagating an `AbortSignal` to give the harness a safety valve.

general_comments.comment: `eval-parallel.ts` is described in the PR architecture section as the primary multi-combo entry point (`node scripts/eval/eval-parallel.ts -p mealdrop` — all 8 combos, 4 models × 2 prompts with live-streamed prefixed logs) but the file does not exist in the diff or in the repository. The PR as merged only ships the single-run `eval.ts`. Either include `eval-parallel.ts` in this PR or update the PR description to reflect what is actually being delivered.

`EVAL_ROOT` in `utils.ts` is hardcoded to `resolve(REPO_ROOT, '..', 'storybook-eval')` — one directory above the repository with a fixed name. This is surprising (results land outside the repo silently) and non-configurable. Consider reading from `process.env.EVAL_ROOT` with the current path as the default, and document the convention with a comment so contributors know where to look for trial results.

The Google Sheets upload path (`EVAL_GOOGLE_SHEETS_URL`) is mentioned in the PR description as a result-upload feature but there is no corresponding implementation in the diff. If this was intentionally deferred, add a TODO comment (with a tracking issue) in `run-trial.ts` near the `summary.json` write step so the gap is visible to future contributors.
